story_text.value:
freehire is a filterable, job board aggregator, job tracker, and AI-assisted resume tailoring tool. Saving your skills and preferences changes which jobs appear and how your resume gets tailored. I've looked at a lot of these solutions over the years and found it really hard to find the right mix of tools in an open-source offering.

I've contributed to a few issues now and worked closely with the maintainer. I've watched this evolve over the last few months. I feel it's ready for everyone to check out and stress test.

Source: github.com/strelov1/freehire

story_text.value:
When GPT-6/Gemini launched recently, a lot of the 3D demos used blender-mcp (https://github.com/ahujasid/blender-mcp). It's cool, but you have to install blender locally and wire up plugins just to try a prompt or share a run.

I built a browser-based 3D mesh playground so you can hook up your own coding agent over MCP (or run in-browser) directly in a tab. It runs on three.js + manifold-3d for blender-like boolean/mesh editing in JS, and gives the agent a render_preview tool to take multi-view screenshots (front/right/top/iso + custom camera angles + clay mode). That way the agent can look at what it built and fix the geometry, similar to how it iterates when building a website.

The submitted link is a trace of Gemini reconstructing a Copenhagen canal scene from a photo: it hits a script error on the first pass, fixes the bug, and then goes through several rounds of checking 4-view and close-up render_preview screenshots to tweak the geometry.

title.value: Show HN: A 3D mesh playground for coding agents (three.js + manifold-3d)

story_text.value:
The SIMD path currently needs arm64 (NEON) and GOEXPERIMENT=simd. I've only benchmarked on an Apple M4, but it should help on any arm64 chip (Graviton, Ampere, etc.). Elsewhere it falls back to a scalar path that does ~300 MB/s, still ahead of cmark and goldmark.

If you know of a faster CommonMark parser, please tell me and I'll add it to the benchmarks.

Under the hood, it borrows a lot from this paper on using simd for json parsing: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.08318

story_text.value:
I originally made this addon 4 years ago, but recently discovered that coding agents love it.

The addon adds a scripting API for Blender’s node trees, such as Geometry Nodes or Shader Nodes.

It generates a function and related types for every node in Blender. Then the agent (or you) can write scripts to create node trees without having to guess what the node, input, and output names are.

It’s meant to be used alongside the Blender MCP.

In my tests, Opus finishes building node trees in at least half the time using at least half the tokens to answer the same prompt.

Because the scripting API forces it to build correct node trees, it has to back track less to fix mistakes. This saves a lot of time and tokens. There is also a skill and some helper functions to let it look up the function signatures for nodes.

Let me know how it works for you!

title.value: Show HN: A Blender addon that makes Claude twice as efficient at using nodes

I’m an avid user of mermaid but am constantly annoyed by their limitation that subgraphs do not follow direction if any internal nodes are connected to the outside. So I asked Claude to add a new syntax called stack layout and it seems to work pretty elegantly.

I also fixed my annoyance with mermaid.live and allowed this playground to save snapshots in your local storage as well. Happy to add more storage features if anyone’s interested!

The one prompt fork is at https://github.com/ramraj07/ra-mermaid

story_text.value:
I created this webpage to compare the rates for trash hauling across the San Francisco Bay Area.

I wanted to see how Oakland California compares to the rest of the region. I knew the rates were high, but I wanted to quantify how high. Especially since the cost of proper trash disposal contributes substantially to Oakland's illegal dumping problem.

I found some interesting insights between wealthiest cities on the peninsula and Oakland, because a city like Atherton actually pays substantially less than Oakland for 20 gallon trash service. I would have expected the operational expenditure related to service delivery to be lower in Oakland, so rates would be lower.

Also, trash hauling has some well-publicized cases of corruption (including the current federal indictment aginst former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao involving waste collection executives).

I think the transparency provided by a webpage like this can only be a good thing.

Please let me know what you think and any feedback.
